extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, reviewers, poets, and students of literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative principles for judging poetry and conducting literary reviews — focusing on what makes poems/poets meritorious and how reviewers should fairly assess and present works. Drawn from a critical essay on Romantic poets and reviewing practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for excellence in humble style
rubrics_metrics.description: An excellent ballad in the humblest style of poetry is to be preferred to twenty indifferent poems that strutted in the highest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value simplicity and genuine excellence over pompous or high-flown verse that lacks merit; the humble form can contain superior poetic power even if its register is low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of superior poetic writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Superior poetic works are characterized by 'greater splendor, a deeper pathos, profounder reflections, and a more sustained dignity of language and of metre.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a poet or a work, look for sustained dignity in diction and metre, the presence of deep feeling (pathos), originality and depth of reflection, and an overarching splendor of execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge by characteristic defects and beauties, not by accidental failures
rubrics_metrics.description: It is vile to decide on the merits of a poet or painter by accidental failures or faulty passages rather than by their characteristic defects or beauties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid basing overall judgment on isolated lapses (the 'knitting-needles and broom-twigs' in a background) or quoting incidental faults as representative; instead, assess recurring, characteristic qualities of the artist's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support critical decisions by fixed canons deduced from human nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should support their decisions 'by reference to fixed canons of criticism, previously established and deduced from the nature of man' rather than by arbitrary dictation or petulant sneers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical judgments ought to appeal to enduring principles (psychological, moral, aesthetic) rather than personal preference, whim, or maliciousness; establish and invoke consistent standards when evaluating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elucidate beauties; pointing out defects alone is limited
rubrics_metrics.description: He who points out and elucidates the beauties of an original work gives the reader interesting information which experience would not have authorized him in anticipating; merely telling me there are defects tells me nothing I should not have taken for granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should prioritize explicating and illuminating what is excellent or original about a work, since this provides readers with substantive, novel insight; mere enumeration of defects is comparatively uninformative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trifling or playful compositions are legitimate if not immoral
rubrics_metrics.description: Compositions which would be enjoyed or passed over according as the taste or humor of the reader might chance to be; provided they contained nothing immoral. The merest trifle had tenfold better claims to its ink and paper than all the silly criticisms on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not condemn light, playful, or minor pieces merely because they are not high art; if they are not immoral, they have a valid place and can serve purposes (amusement, variety) valuable to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid amplifying faults by reprinting worst passages
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics are often 'sure to select and reprint' the passages they deem worthless, thereby 'wast[ing] as much more paper than the author' and magnifying the bad by the greater circulation of reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reprinting isolated poor passages amplifies their reach and can misrepresent the overall work; reviewers should be cautious about giving disproportionate attention to negative excerpts that will spread and shape public judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not apply different rules because an author is dead or alive
rubrics_metrics.description: Why should we judge by a different rule two printed works, only because the one author is alive, and the other in his grave?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain impartial standards across authors regardless of their living status; the same critical criteria should apply to past and present authors alike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess a collection by its whole, not by a few isolated inferior pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: It is hard and unjust to fix the attention on a few separate and insulated poems with as much aversion as if they had been so many plague-spots on the whole work, instead of passing them over in silence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing a collected volume, weigh the balance: a minority of inferior pieces should not be treated as if they nullify the merits of the whole; consider the majority of the work and overall achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial framing and declared choices affect reception
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical remarks prefixed and annexed (the Preface) may be the true origin of unexampled opposition; the omission of less than a hundred lines would have precluded nine-tenths of the criticism. Intentional announcement of certain choices makes defects appear deliberate and provokes hostility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that theoretical statements or prefatory claims by an author can prime readers and critics to judge certain features as intentional and therefore more culpable; authors' self-framing influences critical reception, and critics should try to distinguish intentional experiment from mere ineptitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader variability — same parts may be loved by some and hated by others
rubrics_metrics.description: The same general censure has been grounded by different persons on different poems; 'the composition which one cited as execrable, another quoted as his favorite.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the subjective diversity of taste: critical assessments should allow for the fact that readers bring different habits, prior exposure, and preferences, and that unanimity of judgment is not guaranteed.
